title: Layer-resolved Electronic Structure and Correlation of Low-$n$ Square-planar Nickelates: A DFT+DMFT Prediction of Superconducting Candidates
authors: Jian-Hong She, Rong-Qiang He, Zhong-Yi Lu
abstract: Multi-layer square-planar nickelates provide a rare platform in which the nominal Ni valence, dimensionality, and layer-resolved electronic structure can be tuned within the same structural family. Recent experiments have found superconductivity in $n=4$--8 $R_{n+1}Ni_nO_{2n+2}$ compounds, with the highest $T_c$ near $n=6$, whereas the more heavily hole-doped $n=3$ member remains nonsuperconducting. Here we propose spacer-layer Cl doping as a route to convert low-$n$ nickelates into superconducting candidates. Compared with changing the layer number $n$, Cl substitution on the spacer-layer oxygen sites offers a chemically natural way to continuously tune the Ni valence while leaving the NiO$_2$ planes largely intact; the lower-$n$ compounds may also be more accessible for synthesis. Using density functional theory combined with dynamical mean-field theory, we show that electron-compensated $n=2$ and $n=3$ La-based nickelates, targeted to the nominal Ni valence of superconducting $n=6$, develop Ni-$d$ correlations comparable to those of superconducting higher-$n$ compounds while preserving the characteristic low-energy Ni-$d$ electronic structure. These results suggest spacer-layer Cl doping as a promising strategy for designing low-$n$ square-planar nickelate superconductors.
summary: This theoretical study proposes using spacer-layer Cl doping as a chemical method to induce superconductivity in low-layer number nickelates. By calculating layer-resolved electronic correlations using DFT+DMFT, the authors show that this doping strategy successfully tunes the material's correlation strength to match known superconducting compounds.
main_problem: The study aims to design low-layer number ($n$) square-planar nickelates into superconducting candidates by tuning their electronic structure and correlation strength.
main_result: Spacer-layer Cl doping can drive low-$n$ compounds into a correlated regime comparable to higher-$n$ superconducting nickelates, suggesting it is a promising chemical strategy for material design.
method: The research employs Density Functional Theory combined with Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DFT+DMFT) calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is multi-layer square-planar nickelates ($	ext{R}_{n+1}	ext{Ni}_n	ext{O}_{2n+2}$), focusing on the $	ext{Ni-}d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital. The model uses Cl doping to chemically tune the Ni valence in low-$n$ systems.
key_observables: Layer-resolved electronic structure, correlation strength (quantified by mass enhancement $m^*/m$), and the imaginary part of the Matsubara self-energy ($	ext{Im}\Sigma$).
important_parameters: The layer number ($n=2$ to $6$) and the doping level achieved via Cl substitution are critical parameters.
main_assumptions: It is assumed that spacer-layer Cl substitution provides a chemically natural way to tune valence while keeping the active $	ext{NiO}_2$ planes largely intact.
figures_summary: Figures compare self-energies and mass enhancements across different $n$ values, demonstrating how doping shifts low-$n$ systems towards the correlation regime of high-$n$ superconductors.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the correlation hierarchy in undoped nickelates. It then introduces Cl doping as a tuning mechanism to compensate electrons into low-$n$ compounds, showing that this process successfully induces strong $	ext{Ni-}d$ correlations necessary for superconductivity.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, the use of advanced many-body techniques like DFT+DMFT to map out phase diagrams based on tuning parameters (like doping) shares conceptual overlap with controlling quantum phases in artificial quantum systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Crystal structures of undoped Lan+1NinO2n+2 with n = 3, 4, 5, and 6. The structures consist of square-planar NiO2 blocks separated by spacer layers. Representative inequivalent Ni sites are labeled as Ni1, Ni2, and Ni3 from the outer to the inner NiO2 planes. For the n = 3 structure, the marked spacer-layer oxygen sites indicate the O sites used for O/Cl virtual-crystal substitution.
FIG. 2. Imaginary part of the Matsubara self-energy, ImΣ(iωn), for the Ni-dx2−y2 orbital in undoped Lan+1NinO2n+2 with n = 3–6. Only inequivalent Ni sites are shown.

FIG. 3. Comparison of ImΣ(iωn) for the Ni-dx2−y2 orbital in se- lected undoped La compounds and Cl-doped low-n compounds. The undoped references include La4Ni3O8 (n = 3), La5Ni4O10 (n = 4), and La7Ni6O14 (n = 6). The Cl-doped compounds are treated within VCA and have the same average nominal Ni valence as the undoped n = 6 compound.

FIG. 4. DFT projected band structures and DFT+DMFT spectral functions of representative compounds. The four systems are undoped La4Ni3O8 (n = 3), undoped La7Ni6O14 (n = 6), Cl-doped La3Ni2O5.33Cl0.67, and Cl-doped La4Ni3O7.50Cl0.50. The projected band structures highlight the Ni-dz2 (red) and Ni-dx2−y2 (blue) orbital characters.

FIG. 5. Summary of the layer-resolved Ni-dx2−y2 mass enhancement. (a) Relation between the local Ni-dx2−y2 occupation Nd(dx2−y2) and the effective mass enhancement m∗/m for inequivalent Ni sites in undoped Lan+1NinO2n+2 with n = 3–6. The labels denote (n,Nim), where Ni1, Ni2, and Ni3 are ordered from the outer to the inner NiO2 planes. (b) Comparison of m∗/m across selected undoped and Cl-doped systems. The Cl-doped n = 2 and n = 3 compounds are treated within VCA and have the same average nominal Ni valence as the undoped n = 6 compound.
